results.blind_working: Displacement current is ε0 dΦE/dt. It arises from the time-varying electric flux between the plates, not from charges crossing the gap.
Id = C dV/dt = 2e-6 × 5e4 = 0.1 A
Inside the plates, B = μ0 Id r/(2πR²) = 4πe-7 × 2 × 0.025/(2π × 0.0025) = 4e-6 T
After full charging, the field is constant, so dΦ/dt = 0 and the displacement current is zero. A is false; R is true.
I is false: B is zero on the axis and grows linearly with r inside the plates. II is false: the displacement current equals the conduction current.
Only an accelerated charge produces time-varying fields that radiate. Static charges, uniform motion and steady currents do not radiate.
For a perfect reflector, P = 2I/c = 2(900)/3e8 = 6e-6 N/m^2.
Speed = 1/sqrt(μ0ε0) (III). Average energy density = ½ε0E0² (IV). Intensity = ½ε0cE0² (II). Momentum to an absorbing surface = U/c (I).

A is true: frequency is unchanged. B is false: E0/B0 = v, the speed in the medium, not c. C is true: the electric and magnetic energy densities are equal. D is false: EM waves are uncharged and are not deflected by a magnetic field. E is true: reflection gives 2U/c. So A, C and E.
The Poynting vector E×B must point along +z. Since x̂×ŷ = ẑ, B points along +y.
Here k = π×10^7 m^-1, so λ = 2π/k = 2×10^-7 m. The phase has the form (kz + ωt), so the wave travels along -z.
B0 = E0/c = 30/(3×10^8) = 10^-7 T. The wave travels along +x and E is along ŷ. Since ŷ×ẑ = x̂, B is along +ẑ and in phase with E.
Polarisation needs a transverse wave. EM waves are transverse, while sound in air is longitudinal. Both statements are true, and R explains A.
Statement I is true: S points along the direction of propagation. Statement II is false: the phase (kz + ωt) means travel along -z. When Ex > 0, B must be along -y so that x̂×(-ŷ) = -ẑ.
Frequency increases from microwaves to infrared to ultraviolet to X-rays.
λ = c/ν = 3e8/1.5e18 = 2e-10 m = 0.2 nm, which lies in the X-ray region.
Microwaves are produced by special vacuum tubes such as the klystron and magnetron, and by the Gunn diode.

Radio waves come from accelerated charges in circuits (IV). Infrared comes from hot bodies and molecular vibrations (II). X-rays come from electron bombardment of a metal target (III). Gamma rays come from nuclear decay (I).
A, B and C are true. D is false because all EM waves travel at c in vacuum. E is false because point-contact diodes detect microwaves; infrared is detected by thermopiles and bolometers.
UV radiation kills germs, so it is used to purify drinking water.
f = c/λ = 3×10^8 / 300 = 1 MHz. This lies in the AM band (530–1710 kHz).
Welding goggles protect against UV, not gamma rays, so A is false. Glass absorbs UV, so R is true.

I is false: gamma rays come from nuclear transitions, while X-rays come from inner-shell electron transitions. II: f = 3×10^8 / 3 = 100 MHz. This lies in the FM band (88–108 MHz) and the TV band (54–890 MHz, per NCERT), so II is true.
